questions.q: Describe the main features of the 73rd Amendment relating to local government.
answer: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to rural local government, the Panchayati Raj system, and laid down its main features.

answer.text: It provided a uniform three-tier structure of panchayats at the village, block and district levels, namely the Gram Panchayat, the Panchayat Samiti and the Zilla Parishad. At the base is the Gram Sabha, the assembly of all the voters of a village.

Elections to these bodies are held regularly every five years and are conducted by an independent State Election Commission. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Tribes in proportion to their population, and at least one-third of all seats are reserved for women.
A State Finance Commission is set up every five years to review the financial position of the panchayats.

answer: These features have deepened democracy at the grassroots and empowered weaker sections and women.
